post.description: Creates an unverified account and issues a verification challenge by email. No application data is reachable until verification completes.

201.description: The account was created and a verification email was queued.

400.description: The password does not meet the policy, or the address is malformed.

409.description: The address already holds an account.

post.summary: Register an account with an email address and a password

post.description: Consumes the single-use token from the verification link and activates the account. The token is sent in the body rather than followed as a link so that a mail scanner opening the URL cannot consume it.

400.description: The link is not valid — never issued, already used, expired, or belonging to an account that has itself expired. The four are deliberately indistinguishable.

post.summary: Verify control of a registered email address

post.description: Sends a fresh confirmation link if the address holds an unverified account, and does nothing otherwise. The response is identical in every case, so it cannot be used to discover whether an address is registered.

202.description: Accepted. Empty by design — a body describing what happened would be the disclosure this endpoint exists without.

400.description: The address is malformed. A statement about the request, not about whether an account exists.

post.description: Sends a single-use, time-limited reset link if the address holds a verified account, and does nothing otherwise. The response is identical in every case. Requests are rate-limited per address; a locked account may always request one — consuming the link is what releases the lock.

202.description: Accepted. Empty by design, for the same reason as the verification resend: a body describing what happened would be the disclosure this endpoint exists without.

400.description: The address is malformed. A statement about the request, not about accounts.

429.description: Too many requests for this address in the window. Identical either way.

post.description: Consumes the single-use token and replaces the password. Every existing session for the account is terminated, and a lockout, if one stood, is released. The token is sent in the body rather than followed as a link so a mail scanner cannot consume it. No session is issued: sign in with the new password.

204.description: The password is replaced. Sign in to continue.

400.description: The password does not meet the policy, or the link is not valid — never issued, already used, expired, or superseded by a newer request. The four are deliberately indistinguishable.

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset link

post.description: Verifies the credential and issues a session: a short-lived access token and a single-use refresh token. Failures are uniform for unknown addresses and wrong passwords alike, rate-limited per address, and locked out after repeated failure.

401.description: The email address or the password is not right. Deliberately one answer for both, and for a wrong password on an unverified account.

403.description: The credential is valid but cannot sign in: the address is not verified yet (problem type email-unverified), or the account is locked after repeated failures (problem type account-locked, released by password reset).

429.description: Too many attempts for this address in the window. Identical either way.

post.summary: Sign in with an email address and a password

delete.description: Terminates the session server-side: the refresh token is dead from here on, whatever copies of it exist. Idempotent, and identical for tokens that were never real — signing out is not an endpoint that confirms anything. Signing out of the platform does not end any session at a social identity provider.

204.description: The session is terminated, or already was.

post.description: Rotates the session: the presented refresh token is consumed and a successor pair issued. Presenting an already-consumed token is refused; the session stays bounded by its idle and absolute lifetimes.

401.description: The token is not usable (problem type authentication-required), or the session has reached a lifetime bound (problem type session-expired) — the latter is the signal to re-authenticate in place with work preserved.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a fresh token pair

post.description: UC-68 step one. Verifies email and password; on success the sealed, five-minute factor challenge rides an httpOnly cookie and the body names whose code is now awaited. Failures are uniform for unknown and deactivated operators alike, throttled per address, and locked after repeated failure.

201.description: The credential held; the factor challenge is open and rides the cookie.

401.description: The email address or the password is not right — one answer for both (problem type credential-invalid).

403.description: The operator account is locked after repeated failures (problem type admin-account-locked; released by another administrator or the provisioning CLI).

429.description: Too many attempts for this address in the window. Identical either way.

post.summary: Verify the elevated credential and open the second-factor challenge

post.description: UC-68 step two. Judges the TOTP code against the challenge cookie step one set; on success the session is established as a sealed httpOnly cookie and the challenge is cleared — no token appears in the body (FR-75: the factor is mandatory, without exception).

201.description: The session was established; the cookie carries it.

401.description: No open challenge, or it lapsed (problem type authentication-required — sign-in restarts from the credential); or the code is wrong (problem type factor-invalid, disclosed only past the credential bar — the challenge stays open for a retype).

403.description: The operator account is locked (problem type admin-account-locked) — a wrong code counts toward the same threshold as a wrong password.

429.description: Too many attempts for this address in the window. Identical either way.

post.summary: Complete sign-in with the second factor

get.description: The console router’s probe. Judges the sealed cookie: a live access token answers directly; an expired one is rotated server-side and the successor cookie set on this response. 401 means sign in again.

200.description: The current session, rotated if its access token had expired.

401.description: No usable session (problem type authentication-required), or its lifetimes ran out (problem type session-expired).

delete.description: Revokes the session server-side and clears the cookies — any half-open factor challenge included. Idempotent, and identical for cookies that were never real — signing out is not an endpoint that confirms anything.

204.description: The session is terminated, or already was.

delete.summary: Sign out of the administrative realm

info.title: easyesg API
info.description: One versioned REST surface. Both front ends are ordinary clients of it and no privileged route exists (DR-11, NFR-16). The active organization comes from the session — never from a header, a path segment or a token claim.

status.description: No application data is reachable while an account is unverified (FR-1). An unverified account expires 7 days after registration.

verifiedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. Null while the account is unverified.

email.description: Case is preserved as supplied; uniqueness is case-insensitive.

password.description: Minimum 8 and maximum 128 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one further character. Letters are matched by Unicode property, so Romanian and Russian letters count as letters.

token.description: The value from the verification link. Single-use and valid for 24 hours from issue.

email.description: Malformed addresses are refused as requests; well-formed ones are never.

token.description: The single-use value from the reset link.

password.description: The replacement password, under the same policy as registration: minimum 8 and maximum 128 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one further character.

locale.description: The interface language persisted on the account (FR-10).

accessToken.description: Bearer token for the Authorization header. Signed, short-lived; carries the session identity and no authorization data.

accessTokenExpiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. At most 15 minutes after issuance.

refreshToken.description: Opaque, single-use. Present it to the refresh endpoint to obtain a successor pair; it is invalidated by that refresh, by sign-out, and by a consumed password reset.

refreshTokenExpiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. When this session dies if never refreshed again — the earlier of its idle and absolute bounds.

password.description: Verified against the stored credential; failures are uniform and rate-limited.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token exactly as issued. Single-use: a successful refresh replaces it, and the replaced value is rejected from then on.
The refresh token of the session to terminate. Possession is the authentication: it is what the web tier actually holds, and it keeps sign-out working after the access token has already expired.

expiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. When the challenge lapses and sign-in restarts from the credential (§12.5.6 — five minutes).

password.description: Verified against the elevated credential; failures are uniform and throttled.

role.description: The platform-side actor (actors.md: PA or BO).

expiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. When the session dies if never used again — the earlier of its idle (8 h) and absolute (12 h) bounds.

totpCode.description: The current TOTP code (FR-75 — the second factor is mandatory, without exception).
